notes: family A in-memory state is NOT compact (Vec<f64>/Vec<u16> per row); the bytes saved are the packed state file; per-decision latency is for the in-memory quantised arithmetic
family B bytes are resident heap incl. the router's private vocab + keyword map (as in f3); ids-API rows skip string hashing
timings come from a shared 16 GB box with other workers running: use ratios from interleaved reps, not absolute ns

pre_declared.claim_rule: equivalent in BOTH held-out 31-60 AND confirm 61-90, per world; headline candidates: bf16-sr block-float16 and f16+u16base (family A); SPARSE u16/q16, SPARSE f16/q16, SPARSE f16/f16 (family B)
pre_declared.equivalent_cell_rule: Holm-adjusted TOST p < 0.05 (Holm over all cells of the split) AND 95% CI inside (-margin, +margin)
pre_declared.extension_rule: declared after seeing that n=30/split cannot resolve +-0.005 in the 32-agent worlds: with --ext, fresh seeds 91-250 (n=160) get the same cell rule; separate column, does not rewrite the primary verdict
pre_declared.latency_extra_diagnostic: decode cost = speed vs the SAME implementation/API with f64 cells (compact f64/f64, MiniHeb f64); added because the crate reference is a slower implementation
pre_declared.latency_not_hurt: median decisions/s >= 0.9 x f64 reference in every world
pre_declared.metric: mean expected success over the run (full), paired by seed

references.A: crate Warm<HebbianRouter> (heb_robust_cfg, MeanFeature), verified decision-identical to MiniHeb f64
references.B: crate defaults::recommended_router = Guarded<HebbianRouter>, verified decision-identical to compact f64/f64

pre_declared.tune_split: 1-8 reported for information only; nothing is tuned in this lab (schemes frozen from f2/f3)
